summary: An excerpt from the novel Book 1 (part 137) in which the narrator argues with a companion, Ange, about whether the group should keep jamming, meaning disrupting surveillance, after a crackdown. The narrator is accused of being afraid for himself and walks home after she calls him by the handle M1k3y. He then posts a message to the group saying he will not jam that week or maybe the next, because jamming gets people caught and the DHS will use arrests to catch their friends, and urging them to devise a new tactic. The excerpt ends with the two not speaking for four days.
one_line: In a novel excerpt, the narrator quarrels with Ange over continuing to jam DHS surveillance, then posts that he is stepping back and urges a new tactic.
key_facts: The narrator argues with Ange about whether he is responsible for the group members who look to him for guidance.
Ange accuses the narrator of being afraid they will figure out who he is, and says he is afraid for himself.
Ange calls the narrator 'M1k3y', and the narrator responds, 'Don't call me that!'
The narrator puts on his shoes, picks up his bag, and walks home after the argument.
The posted message says, 'I'm not jamming. Not this week. Maybe not next.'
The message states that jamming is not due to fear but because 'I'm better free than in prison.'
The message says the DHS may use arrested jammers to catch their friends, and their friends' friends.
The message claims, 'It's only jamming if you get away with it.'
The message argues that getting caught makes the DHS look smarter than the group: 'THEY AREN'T SMARTER THAN US!'
The message calls the DHS 'like a maddened bull' that does not worry much about having the right person.
The narrator posts the message, goes to bed, and misses Ange.
Ange and the narrator do not speak for the next four days, including the weekend.

entities.name: M1k3y
